items.title: FirebaseAdmin 3.6.0 deprecates Message.Token in favour of Fid — the version CardiTrack pins; no decommission date yet
items.text:
*FYI* — FirebaseAdmin 3.6.0 deprecates `Message.Token` in favour of `Fid` — the version CardiTrack pins; no decommission date yet
The Firebase Admin .NET SDK v3.6.0 (2026-07-08) has one feature line: "Enable `fid` and deprecate `token` for Send API". `Message.Token`/`MulticastMessage.Tokens` are now obsolete (CS0618) and `Fid`/`Fids` target a Firebase Installation ID instead. Node, Java and Python Admin SDKs shipped the same change within ten days; Google says token targets stay "fully supported until the decommission date" with at least a year's window — and no date is published yet.
Where we stand: `CardiTrack.Infrastructure.csproj` pins exactly 3.6.0, and `FcmNotificationChannel.cs` sends on `Token` under a deliberate CS0618 suppression — correctly, because what `PushDeviceToken` stores is a registration token from Plugin.Firebase's `GetTokenAsync()`, not an Installation ID. Nothing breaks today. Migrating is a paired change (app registers an Installation ID, API stores and sends it) and Plugin.Firebase 4.0.1 exposes no Installations module. Smallest next action: check whether a Plugin.Firebase Installations binding exists for MAUI, and if so start carrying the FID alongside the token in `RegisterPushDeviceRequest` so the server holds both before Google names a date.
https://github.com/firebase/firebase-admin-dotnet/releases/tag/v3.6.0
